mechanism.name: Conditional CDF at (x=5,y=3) in the Henzi-Ziegel-Gneiting clipped-rate Poisson mechanism

generation_equations.label: Source covariate: published Section 4, PDF p.17 / journal p.979, unnumbered paragraph before (23)
Source conditional intensity: published equation (26), PDF p.19 / journal p.981
Source count: published equation (26), PDF p.19 / journal p.981; Y4 renamed Y
generation_equations.expression: Y_i | X_i=x ~ Poisson(lambda(x)), independently across i; P(Y_i=k|X_i=x)=exp(-lambda(x))*lambda(x)^k/k!, k=0,1,...

sampling.dependence: iid observed pairs across rows; within each pair, Y depends on X only through lambda(X). n counts fully observed pairs, not clusters or repeated measurements. No treatment, mediator, missingness, label indicator, censoring or interference mechanism applies.

assumptions: One fully observed pair (X_i,Y_i) per independent identically distributed row; X_i~Uniform(0,10), Y_i|X_i~Poisson(min(max(X_i,1),6)); no missingness, censoring, selection or cross-row dependence.

The conditional kernel is the one defined by equation (26). Because P(X=5)=0, point identification from the joint law uses the continuous-in-x version with positive covariate density around 5; a single zero-probability conditioning event alone does not identify an arbitrary conditional version.

For isotonic interpretation, the usual numerical order of X is used. Nondecreasing clipped intensity implies stochastically increasing conditional laws, hence nonincreasing F_x(y) in x. These properties follow from the DGP and are not causal assumptions.

Uniform design has positive density 0.1 on (0,10); lambda is continuous and 1-Lipschitz, bounded in [1,6]. Poisson coupling gives sup_y |F_x(y)-F_xprime(y)| <= |x-xprime|. After X/10 rescaling, these support the density/order/continuity setting of published Section 2.4 Theorem 3 (PDF pp.12-13 / journal pp.974-975; supplement S2 retains the label Theorem 2.3); this submission proves no estimator rate or confidence-band coverage.

Y is discrete on the nonnegative integers, with finite moments and no Lebesgue density. Positive response-density assumptions for continuous quantiles are inapplicable. No treatment, intervention, exchangeability or mediation condition is imposed.

properties.notes: Only input covariate X; Y is the response, not an extra dimension. X acts through lambda(x)=min(max(x,1),6): constant 1 for x<=1, x on (1,6), constant 6 for x>=6. This is globally non-affine and has kinks at 1 and 6; no product/interaction terms. F_x(3)=exp(-lambda)*(1+lambda+lambda^2/2+lambda^3/6) is nonlinear on (1,6). One active dimension, no padding or high-dimensional confounding; discrete heteroskedastic response with mean=variance=lambda(x). The bounds 1 and 6 truncate the intensity, not Y: the conditional count support is all nonnegative integers and is unbounded above.

estimand.name: theta = F_{Y|X=5}(3)
estimand.definition: P(Y<=3 | X=5) in the source synthetic superpopulation, using its continuous-in-x conditional probability kernel. Inclusive CDF threshold y=3, fixed covariate query x=5, scalar probability in [0,1]. This is conditional, not marginal, and not a quantile or a causal effect.

truth.expression: P(Y<=3 | X=5) in the source synthetic superpopulation, using its continuous-in-x conditional probability kernel. Inclusive CDF threshold y=3, fixed covariate query x=5, scalar probability in [0,1]. This is conditional, not marginal, and not a quantile or a causal effect.
truth.derivation: Finite Poisson PMF sum; Decimal precisions 60/90 audit; separately implemented Gamma(shape=4,rate=1) survival integral over [5,60] by composite Simpson 4096/8192 intervals plus analytic upper-tail bound. Special support, threshold jump and clipped-platform checks.

adaptations: Keep the published Section 4 equation (26) Uniform(0,10) and Poisson(min(max(x,1),6)) law unchanged; rename source response Y4 to observed column Y.
Use the requested fixed scalar conditional CDF P(Y<=3 | X=5). This is a user-selected QDI target, not a numerical result reported by the source, which evaluates distributional predictions by CRPS.

Implement the unjittered equation (26), without the author training-script perturbations X+=Uniform(-1e-6,1e-6) and Y+=Uniform(-1e-6,1e-6) at lines 67-68. This preserves the requested discrete response. Do not claim exact reproduction of the full author preprocessing pipeline.
Use local Python random.Random and a Poisson arrival-count sampler instead of R runif/rpois. Equality in law is intended; R/Python draws are not bitwise identical.
Run only n=128 CPU interface checks and numerical truth checks. Do not reproduce the 500-replicate training/validation experiment, fit predictors, train PFN, or evaluate interval coverage.
